subject: Renewal health & usage — Q3 spike, capacity options, and recommendation
messages:
From: Ariel Soto <ariel@summitai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal health check — Q3 anomalies

Hi Marissa,

We're starting internal renewal planning for SummitAI and noticed a pretty sharp token spike in late August tied to a new feature test. Can you run a renewal health pass for us? Key asks:
- Quick breakdown of Q3 token consumption (daily granularity if possible)
- Any latency regressions or perf anomalies during the spike window
- Options for smoothing cost (burst credits, commit tiers, or short-term headroom)

We'd like to have a call next week to align on options. Tentatively asking for 30 minutes on Oct 5th.

Thanks,
Ariel Soto
Head of Platform, SummitAI
Ariel@summitai.com

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Soto <ariel@summitai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal health check — Q3 anomalies

Hi Ariel — thanks for the note and flagging the spike. We're on it. Attached is a Q3 extraction that breaks down daily token consumption and top endpoints that drove the peak (summitai_q3_usage.csv). Early summary:

- Baseline run-rate (July) ~ 1.2M tokens/day; average August climb to ~1.9M/day with a 3-day peak at 4.1M tokens/day tied to the new async summarization endpoint.
- No latency regressions detected at the model-serving layer; p95 and p99 remained consistent. The majority of delay was client-side retry logic and concurrent fan-out from a new internal worker.
- Cost impact: projected monthly overrun if sustained ~$28k.

Suggested immediate options (short list):
1) Short-term burst credits to cover the August event while you tune client parallelism.
2) A stepped commit (3-month ramp) to reduce per-token unit cost if usage stays high.
3) Apply prefix caching on the summarization calls; our Optimize team estimates 20–35% token savings for your pattern.

I've looped in Ben for pricing/commit options. Can you confirm availability for Oct 5th 11:00am PT? If that doesn't work, suggest two alternate windows.

Attachments: summitai_q3_usage.csv, performance_trends_q3.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0194

---
From: Ariel Soto <ariel@summitai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Kiana Brooks <kiana.b@summitai.com>, infra@summitai.com
Date: 2027-09-30T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal health check — Q3 anomalies

Thanks Marissa — that summary helps. A few clarifications before the call: 
- The spike was an internal beta (non-production) but we want to make sure renewal pricing doesn't penalize us for an isolated test.
- We are keen on prefix caching but concerned about integration complexity with our serverless workers. Any estimated engineering hours?
- For the stepped commit option, what's the quick math for 3-month vs 12-month? We're leaning toward something short-term unless we see a stable uplift.

Confirming Oct 5th 11:00am PT works for Kiana and me. Please include pricing scenarios in the meeting invite.

Appreciate it,
Ariel
---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Soto <ariel@summitai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-01T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal health check — Q3 anomalies

Ariel — looping in Ben and Monica to provide concrete pricing and an implementation estimate. See attached proposed_capacity_options.xlsx (three scenarios) and a one-page performance excerpt (performance_trends_q3.pdf). Key bullets: 

- Short-term (30 days) burst credit: $9,000 one-off credit to cover August-style events and avoid immediate overage charges. No long-term commitment required.
- 3-month stepped commit: commit to 30% uplift over current run-rate for 3 months; blended unit price reduces token cost by ~11% compared to pay-as-you-go. Net new spend estimate (if sustained at August peak) shows paying less than current overage trajectory.
- 12-month commit: best unit economics (approx 21% lower unit price) and includes a one-time onboarding credit; recommended only if you forecast sustained uplift beyond Q4.

Engineering estimate for prefix caching integration: Monica: ~3–6 engineer-days to add an edge-side cache for the summarization flow if you already have an indirection point (lambda / edge worker). If you need SDK-level changes on multiple services, add another 5–7 days. We'll include a short implementation runbook in the call.

Action items for meeting (Oct 5, 11:00am PT):
- Walk through the Q3 usage deck (Marissa)
- Pricing scenarios and draft commitment language (Ben)
- Implementation plan and engineer-day estimate for caching (Monica)

Meeting link: https://meet.redwood.com/rc/xyz-123

Attachments: proposed_capacity_options.xlsx

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---
From: Kiana Brooks <kiana.b@summitai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Ariel Soto <ariel@summitai.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal health check — Q3 anomalies

Marissa / Ben / Monica — thanks for the clear options and the implementation estimate. We discussed internally and would like to: 

1) Accept the 30-day burst credit to cover the August test while we complete tuning.
2) Pilot the 3-month stepped commit at the 30% uplift level starting Oct 15 to evaluate whether the uplift sustains. If after 60 days run-rate is still above our Q2 baseline, we will consider converting to a 12-month commit.

We'll accept the engineer-day estimate for prefix caching; our infra lead will join the kickoff for implementation. Please send a short SOW and draft amendment for the 3-month stepped commit and the one-off burst credit.

Thanks — see you on the call.

Kiana Brooks
Director, Product Operations | SummitAI
kiana.b@summitai.com

Attachments referenced: none in this reply.
